oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Coauthoring Library Instruction with Writing Faculty: A Case Study of the Train-the-Trainer Model
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Taylor Moorman
Jacqueline Frank
Star Bradley
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Academic libraries can struggle to offer consistent, sustainable information literacy instruction across survey courses with large numbers of sections and students. This case study presents an innovative train-the-trainer model at Montana State University that integrated library instruction into a first-year survey course. When faced with trials of capacity for a first-year writing program, librarians partnered with writing program administrators to revamp the library’s approach and reach over 1,100 students across 57 sections during a semester. While initial conversations revealed opposing priorities, librarians pivoted to an alternative collaborative model to satisfy both sides. This resulted in developing instructor training sessions, complete with learning materials created by librarians. The authors discuss finding commonality amidst differing ideals and share insights into the collaborative process. Assessment data proves the model effective, with positive outcomes reported. This approach offers a template for academic libraries seeking to expand instructional reach in a sustainable way. Keywords: Information literacy instruction, faculty-librarian collaboration, faculty development, faculty outreach, teach-the-teacher, train-the-trainer, scalable instruction, first-year seminar, first-year writing program
